description: We are a university team from Quito with skills in AI, software, electronics and networking & telecom. We chose Challenge 9, The Earth Information Jukebox: turning NASA Earth visualizations into sound and music, so people who cannot see them can still hear how our planet changes. We compete virtually but meet in person in Quito. We are looking for someone from music or acoustic engineering to help make the data sound like music, not noise. Join us!
summary:
Resonant Earth turns NASA Earth data visualizations into sound, so blind and low-vision people can "listen" to how our planet changes. We built a pipeline that reads each frame of a NASA video, extracts features (average value, area, position) and maps them to pitch, volume and stereo pan: the hotter the data, the higher the note. Our web app, "Listen to the Earth", offers two real tracks: global temperature 1880-2023 (NASA GISTEMP) and ocean temperature and currents 2007-2008 (SVS/ECCO2).

Its centerpiece is Eco, a bilingual (English/Spanish) voice guide powered by AI. Eco introduces the site, explains what you hear using only the real data, answers free-form questions, highlights the part of the page it is talking about, and gives a guided tour of both tracks. It works by voice ("Hey Eco"), keyboard, or text, and it avoids double voices with screen readers.

It matters because climate data is mostly visual. Sound makes it accessible, memorable and explorable for everyone.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Resonant Earth turns NASA Earth-science visualizations into sound. A Python pipeline takes a NASA video, reads each frame, converts the color bar back into data values (CIE Lab color matching), extracts features per frame (mean value, area, centroid position, change) and maps them to musical notes: the higher the value, the higher the pitch; area controls volume; horizontal position controls stereo pan. The output is an MP4 with the generated audio. Our website, "Listen to the Earth", plays two real tracks: global temperature 1880-2023 (NASA GISTEMP) and ocean temperature and currents 2007-2008 (SVS/ECCO2), with a chart, a live reading of the data at every moment, and an accessible description of each track.

ECO, THE AI VOICE GUIDE

Eco is a bilingual (English/Spanish) guide that lives on the page. It introduces the project, explains what you are hearing using only the real data of the current moment, answers free-form questions, highlights and scrolls to the part of the page it is talking about, presses the controls for you, and gives a guided tour of both tracks. It can be activated with the "Talk to me" button, the H key, or by saying "Hey Eco". Without AI, it still works with simple commands.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Climate data is almost always presented visually. Sound makes it accessible to blind and low-vision people and gives everyone a new, memorable way to explore it. Eco removes the need to find and understand controls, so people can simply ask.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

Python and ffmpeg (data pipeline and audio), HTML/CSS/JavaScript with ES modules, Three.js and GSAP (3D globe and animations), the Web Audio API, the Web Speech API (voice recognition and synthesis), Cloudflare Workers (a small intermediary service that keeps the API key secret) and Google Gemini (language model for Eco).

CREATIVITY

We treat data as music and add a guide that behaves like a person working in the page: it speaks, points, and presses buttons, so users do not have to guess where to look.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Accessibility (full keyboard use, always-visible captions, no double voices with screen readers, automated accessibility checks with zero violations, reduced-motion support); honesty (the ocean track is a relative index, not real degrees, and Eco says so); privacy (the microphone only opens after a user action, a clear notice says phrases are sent to an AI service, AI answers are labeled, the API key is never in the website); and resilience (if the AI is slow, saturated or offline, the guide falls back to local commands). Eco's AI answers are labeled "generated by AI" in the interface, and the team logo carries a visible watermark.
